# ChatGPT Subscription
**English** | **中文**
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that connects your ChatGPT account through OpenAI's sign-in page and lets
you use the account's available ChatGPT models inside DSH. You need an account with Codex access and
sufficient quota. The plugin does not reject Free accounts, but sign-in alone does not establish ac
cess to models in DSH; availability depends on OpenAI’s plan, client and model restrictions. See Ope
nAI’s current plan information.
## What it does
Sign in from the plugin page, then select a model under the **ChatGPT** provider. The plugin maintai
ns the sign-in and shows account status, expiry, and **Sign in again / Unbind** actions. Available m
odels depend on your account and DSH's model support.
The companion Bottom Info Bar displays available quota windows and reset times. Both plugins can be
installed independently; ChatGPT quota display needs a valid sign-in.

## Settings
Open **Plugins → ChatGPT Subscription** and choose **Sign in with ChatGPT**. Complete authorization
in the browser; when the page shows **Connected**, select a ChatGPT model in the conversation model
picker. Allow DSH pop-ups if the authorization page does not open.
The browser confirms success only after the plugin has saved the sign-in and connected it to DSH. If
that fails, return to the plugin page for the error; do not share sign-in files or authorization UR
at fails, return to the plugin page for the error; do not share sign-in files or authorization URLs.
**Sign in again** renews the binding. **Unbind** disconnects the account from this plugin. An existi
ng Codex CLI sign-in is not automatically adopted by the plugin.
## Sign-in data and updates
Authorization and model requests communicate with official OpenAI endpoints. Sign-in tokens are save
d in the standard local `~/.codex/auth.json` file with owner-only permissions and synchronized into
DSH's credential store. Signing in can update that shared file, so it can affect which account Codex
CLI uses. Tokens are transmitted to OpenAI for authorized requests; they are not written to plugin
uses. Tokens are transmitted to OpenAI for authorized requests; they are not written to plugin logs.
Unbinding and uninstalling preserve `~/.codex/auth.json` and remove the plugin's binding and managed
DSH entries. The plugin refreshes sign-in automatically. Under **Version and updates**, automatic u
pdates (default) check npm when DSH starts, verify and replace the plugin files, then take effect af
ter a restart. Manual mode checks without installing; installation asks for confirmation. Failed upd
ates restore the previous files, and settings offer rollback when needed. Sign-in data is preserved.
Local checkout and linked installs require a code update and rebuild; see docs/INSTALL.md.
## Uninstall and roll back
Remove the plugin from the desktop app's **Plugins** page, or use `dsh plugin --profile web remove d
sh-chatgpt-sub` for the CLI web profile, then restart DSH. Uninstalling keeps `~/.codex/auth.json` (
the Codex CLI's own sign-in) and removes this plugin's binding and the DSH entries it manages. To go
back a version instead of removing the plugin, **Version and updates** offers rollback after a fail
ed update or while a newer build waits for a restart. Do not include sign-in files, credentials, or
account details in bug reports.
## Languages
The plugin includes English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Portugue
se, French, German, Italian, Russian, Hindi and Indonesian. It follows DSH’s language by default. Ch
oose **Language** on this plugin’s settings page to use a different language independently; the choi
ce is saved in this browser. Regional variants such as Spanish (Mexico) and Portuguese (Brazil) use
the corresponding built-in language. Unsupported languages fall back to English.
## Development

- Build: `npm run build`
- Test: `node tests/run-all.mjs`
